theme: 3 terms on how long an object lives: the span from creation to release, a function that keeps an object alive through a closure, and a reference that skips automatic memory management

terms.definition: The time between creating a class instance and freeing it, which ends when no strong reference is left.
terms.example: Check the Object Lifetime here, the cache outlives the screen that made it.

terms.definition: A function that keeps an object alive at least until the closure you pass it has finished.
terms.example: Wrap the call in withExtendedLifetime, or the delegate might be freed too early.

terms.definition: A wrapper for a class reference that skips automatic retain and release, so you manage the memory yourself.
terms.example: The C callback only takes a raw pointer, so we pass the view model through Unmanaged.

video.title: Object Lifetime, withExtendedLifetime & Unmanaged | Day 72
video.description:
Learn to explain how long objects live in Swift: Object Lifetime, withExtendedLifetime & Unmanaged, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Object Lifetime - The time between creating a class instance and freeing it, which ends when no strong reference is left.
withExtendedLifetime - A function that keeps an object alive at least until the closure you pass it has finished.
Unmanaged - A wrapper for a class reference that skips automatic retain and release, so you manage the memory yourself.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: Swift Object Lifetime, withExtendedLifetime & Unmanaged | Day 72
landscape.description:
Explain Object Lifetime, withExtendedLifetime & Unmanaged in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
객체 수명, withExtendedLifetime, Unmanaged 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Object Lifetime - The time between creating a class instance and freeing it, which ends when no strong reference is left.
한국어: 객체 수명: 클래스 인스턴스가 만들어져서 해제될 때까지의 시간으로, 강한 참조가 하나도 남지 않으면 끝남

withExtendedLifetime - A function that keeps an object alive at least until the closure you pass it has finished.
한국어: withExtendedLifetime: 넘겨준 클로저가 끝날 때까지 객체가 최소한 살아 있도록 보장하는 함수

Unmanaged - A wrapper for a class reference that skips automatic retain and release, so you manage the memory yourself.
한국어: Unmanaged: 자동 retain과 release를 건너뛰는 클래스 참조 래퍼로, 메모리 관리를 직접 해야 함

In this video, Mina and Jake ask why a call is wrapped in a closure, find out that scope is not the same as lifetime and see what an Unmanaged reference does not do, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Still in scope, but already freed? Can you explain it in English?

dialogue.title: In scope, but alive?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, why does `run` wrap `send` in withExtendedLifetime?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Because `send` only gets an Unmanaged reference. That doesn't keep `s` alive.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: But `s` stays in scope until the closing brace.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Scope isn't Object Lifetime. Swift only promises `s` lives until its last use.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. After that, Swift may free `s`, even inside `run`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So `send` might get a freed object?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. withExtendedLifetime keeps `s` alive until the closure finishes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then why use Unmanaged at all? Just pass `s`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: C APIs often want a raw pointer. Unmanaged gives one with no retain, so Object Lifetime is our job.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Unmanaged doesn't hold it, so withExtendedLifetime has to.
Scope isn't Object Lifetime, Swift can free it after its last use.
